SMTO-EXE-0079 — SMTO can't tell whether your clipboard was changed

GUID: 1db9625b-f9cf-5c81-b618-c8b8b4e97a1f
Slug: clipboard-outcome-unknown
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: clipboard

What happened

  • SMTO asked the Gateway computer to copy something to its clipboard, or to clear it, but lost the answer partway through. The clipboard may or may not have changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the Gateway computer, paste into a blank note or text box to see what the clipboard holds now. The change may already have happened, and doing it again could overwrite something you wanted.
  2. If the clipboard already holds what you asked for, you're done; don't ask SMTO to repeat it. SMTO doesn't repeat clipboard changes by itself, so nothing else will overwrite it.
  3. If it doesn't, open Settings › Setup › Gateways, select Check connection for that Gateway, then ask SMTO for the change once more. A dropped connection or a stuck clipboard step is the usual cause, so confirm the Gateway answers first.

What success looks like

  • Pasting on that computer shows exactly the content you wanted, and any new request is reported as completed.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway, noting what you saw when you pasted. Don't include the clipboard contents themselves in the report.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A clipboard write or clear may have changed the selected Gateway's clipboard before its native, worker or transport receipt failed, so the effect is unknown.

What this means

  • A clipboard write/clear may have changed ownership or content before its native, worker or transport receipt failed. These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.

Why this can happen

  • A clipboard write/clear may have changed ownership or content before its native, worker or transport receipt failed.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original execution receipt and current format/change metadata; read content only if explicitly requested.

How to fix it

  • Do not replay the write. Correlate the execution_id in the Server and Gateway logs, run clipboard.inspect (metadata only) on the same Gateway to compare change_id and formats, and read content only if the user explicitly asks. Investigate the failing layer (wl-copy/xclip exit on Linux, isolated clipboard_worker failure or deadline on Windows/macOS, or transport loss) before authorizing a new write.
  • Do not repeat the write automatically. Inspect current formats and, only if requested, read content on the same Gateway before deciding a next action.

Retry and execution caution

  • Do not repeat the write automatically. Inspect current formats and, only if requested, read content on the same Gateway before deciding a next action.

How to verify the fix

  • The original write or clear is reconciled before deciding whether any further mutation is needed.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain clipboard write or include content in diagnostics.

Technical notes

  • These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
